# `get_go_cmd`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Capture a wide-camera image, locate the Sun or Moon and return movement commands as a string.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd2940, CalcGoPlanetCmd @0x226aa0 (64-bit build) |

Takes no parameters. Starts the video stream on the wide camera, waits for an image, detects the Sun or Moon, computes pixel deltas and builds movement command strings, then stops the stream. The commands are not executed. The result is a string, not an object; each command is followed by `;` (so a non-empty result ends with `;`), and it can be empty when there are no command elements. Each command has the form `:Mp±NNNNNN:±NNNNNN#`, two signed offsets in arcseconds zero-padded to six digits (READ). The offsets are consecutive steps, each relative to the previous point (INFERRED); which mount axis each field drives is unresolved. The 64-bit build fails unless the model is one of the three supported ones (S30 Plus, S30, S50) and the expected wide camera is selected. On S30 Plus-class units the ScanSun worker fetches this list from the peer unit after its first goto and sends each command to the mount. Capture is started and stopped on both builds, so the method is not observation-only despite the getter name; a client MUST NOT call it as a passive query. No event is emitted.

Side effects: Starts and stops camera streaming for the duration of the call; the wait for an image is bounded by roughly the exposure time plus five seconds.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_go_cmd"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 207 | Unsupported model, wrong camera, no subframe, stream start or image wait failure, detection or delta failure; most early failures only log, so the default applies | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Lower detection, delta and camera code sets are unresolved; no per-condition code is assigned. The success example uses invented offsets.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"get_go_cmd"}
```

Reply, success:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_go_cmd","result":":Mp+000120:-000045#;:Mp+000060:+000010#;","code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_go_cmd","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"id":82}
```
